chains.trait: Eight jointed legs grip smooth basalt

skill.effect: The spider clings firmly to vertical stone surfaces and senses nearby movement through the ground. You can hear its subtle vibrations before it strikes.

chains.weakness: Disoriented by loud, sudden roars that mask tremors

journal.en: It watches the rock for footsteps.

plausibility.summary: At 1.05 g (F2), a wall-clinging ambusher needs strong attachment on steep lava-tube basalt (F9); andesite/basalt transmits seismic surface waves efficiently, so substrate vibration is a credible prey cue. ~180 g at ~5 cm prosoma scale matches very large mygalomorph spiders on Earth (mass is high but within what elevated pO₂ (D10/F5) and island gigantism (F27/D30) can pay for in tracheal oxygen delivery—Graham et al. on Palaeozoic hyperoxia and insect size.
fixes: At 1.05 g (F2), a wall-clinging ambusher needs strong attachment on steep lava-tube basalt (F9); andesite/basalt transmits seismic surface waves efficiently, so substrate vibration is a credible prey cue. ~180 g at ~5 cm prosoma scale matches very large mygalomorph spiders on Earth (mass is high but within what elevated pO₂ (D10/F5) and island gigantism (F27/D30) can pay for in tracheal oxygen delivery—Graham et al. on Palaeozoic hyperoxia and insect size.

analogues.organism: Tarantulas and amblypygids (whip spiders): scopulae/claws on rock, vibration-sensitive slit sensilla and leg microtrichobia for prey localization.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Silk snare spun across cave fissures
links: D11 dense air reduces drag on strands
D8 thick atmosphere keeps nets from sagging

skill.effect: It weaves a thick silk trap across narrow passages to strongly pin struggling creatures. You must quickly sever the strands before the catch takes hold.

chains.weakness: Flammable; wind or fire breaks the web

journal.en: It waits in the dark, net ready.

plausibility.summary: Derive sag control from short fissure spans, high-tension cribellate or flagelliform silk, and very humid air slowing protein-thread drying—not from reduced drag. Mention opportunistic spans across cave breathing vents where airflow is predictable at dawn/dusk.
fixes: Derive sag control from short fissure spans, high-tension cribellate or flagelliform silk, and very humid air slowing protein-thread drying—not from reduced drag. Mention opportunistic spans across cave breathing vents where airflow is predictable at dawn/dusk.

analogues.organism: Meta menardi and allied cave orb-weavers; net-casting spiders (Deinopis) for fissure-spanning snares.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Active only at dawn and dusk
links: D19 wind force drives surface detritus

skill.effect: The creature lies in wait during twilight hours and strikes swiftly from the shadows. You must watch carefully for its sudden lunge as light fades or breaks.

chains.weakness: Hides or freezes in bright midday light
observe: Strikes as surface sounds drift in

plausibility.summary: Tie the schedule explicitly to prey commute and cave-mouth airflow/stack-effect reversal at twilight, not D19 moon tides or generic 'wind drives detritus' (weak for an in-cave trapper).

links: D10 high oxygen fuels rapid chitin repair
F15 humid air slows cuticle drying

skill.effect: Its dark shell holds moisture tightly, allowing it to endure arid conditions without tiring. The carapace quickly repairs itself after being struck.

chains.weakness: Overheats if exposed to direct sun or vents

journal.en: It drinks the air through its shell.

relations.note: Primary decomposer; rich in gut contents and symbionts.
Scavenges snared individuals or competes for carcasses.

body_plan.origin: arthropod-like, evolved independently from the seed's porphyrin-based DNA

moments: When a carcass drifts from the shallows into the flooded cave, the entire colony drops their nets in unison, vibrating the basalt like a struck bell.
